name: comparator-offset-mc
description: Monte-Carlo input-referred offset of the comparator front end over PVT, plus the part of that offset that moves across a +/-50 mV input-common-mode band, plus a null control showing this PDK models no resistor local mismatch.
claim: HARNESS PLUMBING ONLY while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder. Once a real design/ netlist is bound, this bench substantiates README.md#target-specification's Offset-sigma row (<= 15 mV 3-sigma input-referred, <= 8 mV stretch) -- measured, not asserted, via gf180mcu's sw_stat_mismatch local-mismatch models.

sig_vos_mv.description: MISMATCH-ON GUARD, not a spec bound. design.ngspice defaults sw_stat_mismatch = 0, so a deck that failed to turn local mismatch on would report ~0 here while every other number in the record still looked plausible. 0.05 mV is far below anything a real 180 nm input pair can achieve, so this floor cannot be read as a design assertion -- it only catches a collapsed (mismatch-free) population. The SPEC bound (<= 15 mV 3-sigma, README.md) is deliberately NOT encoded as a check while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder: a placeholder passing or failing a spec row would be meaningless either way.

av_sigma_pct.description: LOAD-BEARING SELF-CHECK, not a design number. Each draw's gain is taken as (DC point at +2 mV minus DC point at 0 mV) within ONE `dc` sweep, which is only valid if the Monte-Carlo draw is constant across that sweep. If the draw were re-rolled per sweep point, (dv1 - dv0) would be dominated by the difference of two independent offsets rather than by the 2 mV probe, and the extracted gain would scatter by tens of percent. A few percent here is the proof that the draw was preserved, and therefore that every V_os in this record is a real offset rather than a difference of two populations.

sig_rpair_uv.description: NULL CONTROL: 1-sigma resistance mismatch of two identical ppolyf_u_1k loads, read as 1 uA times their difference. EXPECTED TO BE ZERO. gf180mcu wires `*(1+mis_r*sw_stat_mismatch)` into every resistor subckt but hard-sets mis_r = 0 and leaves the area-scaled agauss expression commented out, so this PDK models no resistor local mismatch at all. That means the offset sigma above contains NO load-mismatch contribution and that term must be budgeted by hand. As a live check rather than a comment it is a regression guard: a PDK revision that switches mis_r on fails here instead of silently changing every offset record in this repo.

mean_vos_sem.description: SYMMETRY CHECK, expressed in standard errors of the mean so it is independent of whatever sigma the bound DUT happens to have. The population mean offset must be ~0 because the circuit is nominally symmetric; +/-5 standard errors is a ~6e-7 two-sided false-alarm rate at this N. A mean outside it means a systematic asymmetry is riding on top of the mismatch -- a netlist error, or a genuinely asymmetric topology.

vbias_anchor_mv.description: CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR. The bias pin's own voltage is a V_th proxy and is strongly corner- and temperature-dependent, unlike the mismatch sigma above, which is corner-invariant almost by construction (A_Vt lives in the PDK's fets_mm subcircuits, not in any corner section). Without an anchor this manifest would have nothing that could fail under `--sabotage-corners`, and its headline numbers would stay 'valid' with the corner runner stuck on typical. It is deliberately measured on `ibn`, a CONTRACT node (the DUT's ibias pin), not on an internal node, so it survives a DUT swap. Floors calibrated from the full 45-point mos grid measured in this experiment's first committed record (named in this experiment's README.md), with ~45 % margin below the observed weakest slice, following the sibling repo's calibrate-from-a-cited-clean-tree-record convention. Observed weakest slices there: process 27.35 %, temperature 14.76 %. The supply axis is deliberately unfloored: a diode-connected mirror's gate voltage is set by the forced bias current and is essentially supply-independent by design, so a floor there would fail for a correct circuit.

evidence.mc_seed: ngspice `setseed 20260909` at the top of the control block, then 200 draws per PVT point via `reset` inside a `dowhile` loop (each reset re-evaluates the agauss expressions in the PDK's fets_mm subcircuits). The SAME seed is used at every PVT point -- common random numbers -- so movement of the reported sigma across the grid is a real PVT effect and not sampling noise; N for statistical-error purposes is 200, not 200 x 45. `setseed <n>` is the only ngspice seeding control that works for this: `set rndseed` is silently ignored and `.options seed` freezes the draw.
evidence.mc_scope: mismatch-only (sw_stat_mismatch = 1, sw_stat_global left at the PDK default 0). Global process variation is swept deterministically by the corner axis instead, so the two are never confounded in one number.
evidence.mc_sigma: 1-sigma of the input-referred offset is reported directly, alongside the 3-sigma value README.md's offset row is stated at. Statistical precision on each sigma is 1/sqrt(2N) = 5.0 % at N = 200. Offset per draw is -dv(0 mV)/A_v where A_v is measured on the SAME draw from the 0 mV and +2 mV points of one `dc` sweep; av_sigma_pct is the check that the draw really was preserved between them.
notes: TWO DC POINTS PER DRAW, ONE INSTANCE. Gain is measured inside a single `dc` sweep of the shared differential source, not from a second instance. Two instances would have independent mismatch draws, so their difference would contain an offset difference rather than just the gain.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS RECORD. (a) The decision stage's own offset -- it has no DC operating point, so this method cannot reach it at all; referred to the comparator input it is divided by the gain measured here, and closing it needs either a transient Monte Carlo or an A_Vt-based derivation once the topology is decided. (b) Load-resistor mismatch, which this PDK does not model at all (see the sig_rpair_uv null control). (c) Any layout-induced systematic offset -- this is a schematic-level record.

THE COMMON-MODE BAND IS +/-50 mV ABOUT dut_vcm AND IT IS A STANDALONE CHOICE. gf180-sar-adc's equivalent bench sweeps the band its CDAC produces; there is no CDAC here, so the band is a stated property of the comparator's own input range rather than inherited from a driving circuit.
